title: Create staged-fallback + emergency-throttle runbook and implement headroom quotas after dedicated fleet shortfall
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: This ticket captures the post-incident engineering work after a dedicated-fleet capacity shortfall on 2026-02-28 that surfaced as sustained 95th/99th latency spikes and quota errors for 12 customers. We will implement a staged-fallback orchestration (graceful throttling -> model-variant fallback -> cross-region routing), emergency throttling controls, per-customer headroom quotas, and a detailed runbook for on-call and SRE to reduce time-to-mitigation for future events.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC: First increase in 99th percentile latency observed on dedicated-us-west-2; 03:17 UTC: error rate to customers started increasing (429/503); 03:22 UTC: autoscaler failed to scale due to control-plane API timeouts; 03:35 UTC: fallback to spare pools partially mitigated throughput but introduced increased cold-start latencies; 04:05 UTC: manual emergency throttle applied for top-10 noisy customers; 05:10 UTC: traffic reshaped and stabilised; total customer-facing impact window ~02:12 - 05:40 UTC for some tenants. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood-internal/alerts/DED-20260228
root_cause: A kernel scheduling optimization (PR #7832) introduced an edge case where long tail sequence lengths caused inaccurate capacity estimations in the autoscaler estimator. That combined with a spike in multi-tenant prefix cache misses during a model rollout led to abrupt queue growth. The autoscaler then hit an external provisioning timeout when creating replacement workers because the node template used a new image with a delayed startup hook.
immediate_mitigations: 1) Scoped rollback of kernel scheduling change (PR #7832 reverted) to restore estimator behavior. 2) Emergency throttle: per-customer egress throttles applied to the top-10 throughput customers. 3) Manual allocation of warm spare pools in us-west-2 and us-east-1 to absorb burst. 4) Increased provisioning timeout threshold for node API calls to avoid cascade failures.
follow_up_action_items: Create and publish a staged-fallback orchestration design doc (owner: @Liam Patel) — include throttle -> variant-fallback -> cross-region routing policy and SLO-preserving heuristics
Implement per-customer headroom quotas and a lightweight quota enforcement API (owner: @Anya Rodriguez) — target rollout in dedicated-2.9
Add an autoscaler estimator unit-test harness that replays sequence-length distributions from production for regression testing (owner: @Ravi Menon)
Add a cross-check in CI that prevents autoscaler estimator regressions by validating capacity outputs against historical traffic profiles (owner: @Sergio Kim)
Update the Dedicated fleet runbook with an "Emergency Throttle" section, step-by-step playbook and escalation matrix (owner: @Maya Chen) — link runbook: https://confluence.redwood/dedicated-runbook
Introduce 'warm-spare' pool policy and automated warm-up signals to avoid cold starts on emergency allocations (owner: @Priya Nair)
Schedule a postmortem review with top affected customers and CS to share findings and mitigation timeline (owner: @Ethan Lowe)
Instrument per-tenant prefix cache hit metrics and expose them in Console per-route panels (owner: @Leila Hassan)
Backport the autoscaler hotfix and test against a synthetic spike test in staging (owner: @Ravi Menon)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbook published and validated with SRE on-call run through (documented exercises). 2) Per-customer headroom quota implemented and enabled behind a feature flag; unit+integration tests passing. 3) Autoscaler estimator has non-regression tests that cover the sequence-length distributions observed in the incident. 4) Console surfaces per-tenant cache-hit and throttling signals for customers. 5) Emergency throttle API deployable within 5 minutes by on-call.
test_plan:
- Add replay tests that use anonymized production traces for sequence length and KV cache hit/miss patterns.
- Create a chaos-test scenario in staging: autoscaler disabled + synthetic spike in 95th token-rate to validate staged-fallback flows.
- Runbook tabletop with SRE and SG (simulate node API timeouts) and capture time-to-mitigate metrics.
- E2E test of emergency throttle API against 10k concurrent connections in a dedicated staging pool.
notes_and_discussion:
- Engineering lead sign-off requested for the headroom quota schema.
- Design trade-off: per-customer quotas add operational overhead but give predictable isolation vs complex cross-tenant throttling rules. PM recommended starting with a conservative default headroom of 20% and making it configurable per-customer.
- On-call feedback: need one-click emergency throttle in Console; current CLI-only flow is too slow.
- Security: quota metadata stored encrypted; no user data exposure expected. Security review flagged audit logging for throttle events which is scheduled as separate follow-up.
- Timeline for rollout suggested: feature-flagged pilot to 5 customers in dedicated staging by 2026-03-15, GA to all dedicated tenants in dedicated-2.9 release.
